title: Building a banking regime for the future - speech by David Bailey
summary: David Bailey of the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) outlined the PRA's current pipeline of reforms related to banking sector capital and liquidity regulation at a JP Morgan UK Banks ALM Conference. The speech emphasizes that the regulatory framework is being updated to balance resilience, efficiency, proportionality, and innovation support. Key milestones include the implementation of Basel 3.1 standards (published January 2026, effective start of 2027) and ongoing evolution of the ring-fencing regime. The speech frames regulation as supporting growth by maintaining trust in the UK financial system, operating efficiently, and being responsive to innovation.
key_points: PRA requires banks to hold capital to absorb unexpected losses, support customers through downturns, and enable orderly failure while protecting taxpayers
The UK banking system is stated to be twenty times leveraged, making banks inherently vulnerable to confidence shocks and maturity mismatches
Basel 3.1 standards were published in January 2026, with firms given until start of 2027 to implement
UK introduced ring-fencing regime separating core retail banking from wholesale and investment activities within groups
Secondary objective to facilitate competitiveness and growth came into effect in 2023
Strong and Simple regime introduced as part of proportionality efforts
Three regulatory foundations supporting growth: maintaining trust/resilience, operating efficiently, and being responsive to innovation
Post-crisis resilience building phase is considered complete; focus now shifting to efficiency and proportionality
why_it_matters: This speech provides forward guidance on UK banking regulation that will affect how banks structure their balance sheets, capital buffers, and liquidity reserves. Market participants need to understand how evolving PRA requirements may change the cost of banking operations and affect competitive dynamics between UK and international banks. The balance between resilience and proportionality signals potential changes to capital requirements that could free up resources for lending or investment.
macro_context: The speech discusses how banking regulation supports sustainable economic growth by maintaining financial stability and enabling efficient capital allocation. Bailey emphasizes that regulatory requirements directly support the PRA's primary objective of safety and soundness while also facilitating the UK's role as a major global financial centre. The secondary objective of supporting competitiveness and growth came into effect in 2023.
market_structure_context: The speech discusses the structural separation through ring-fencing (core retail vs. wholesale/investment activities), Basel 3.1 implementation timelines, and the PRA's approach to ensuring orderly failure mechanisms that protect the broader financial system from bank failures.
